questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: The commonest micronutrient deficiency in Bangladesh, especially in women of reproductive age and young children.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Stunting, wasting and underweight in under-fives remain a major public health problem in Bangladesh.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Vitamin K is made by gut flora and widely available in green vegetables; deficiency is mainly a neonatal issue, not a population-level problem.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Obesity is an emerging problem of overnutrition, not a nutritional deficiency.

questions.pearl: Major nutritional problems in Bangladesh: PEM, iron deficiency anaemia, vitamin A deficiency, iodine deficiency disorders and zinc deficiency.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Listeria monocytogenes is a Gram-positive, motile (tumbling motility) bacillus.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Corynebacterium diphtheriae is a Gram-positive club-shaped bacillus arranged in Chinese-letter pattern.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Staphylococci are Gram-positive cocci in grape-like clusters, not bacilli.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Escherichia coli is a Gram-negative bacillus.

questions.pearl: Gram-positive bacilli: Clostridium, Corynebacterium, Listeria, Bacillus (and Actinomyces, Nocardia).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Scabies spreads by direct skin-to-skin contact, the classic contagious disease in Park.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Trichomoniasis is a sexually transmitted infection spread by direct contact; STDs are classic contagious diseases.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pulmonary TB is airborne (droplet nuclei), so it is infectious/communicable but not contagious in the strict sense of transmission by contact.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Malaria is vector-borne via the female Anopheles mosquito, not spread by contact.

questions.pearl: Park: a contagious disease is transmitted by direct contact, e.g. scabies, trachoma, STDs and leprosy.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Arteriolar vasodilatation (histamine, NO) increases blood flow, causing heat and redness.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Endothelial contraction opens gaps in venules, allowing protein-rich exudate to escape.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Margination, rolling, adhesion and transmigration bring neutrophils to the site of injury.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Not one of the three cardinal components (vascular changes, permeability, leukocyte emigration); it is the trigger rather than the process itself.

questions.pearl: Three major components of acute inflammation: vasodilatation, increased vascular permeability and leukocyte emigration.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sandal gap is a classic feature of Down's syndrome.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Flat facial profile with flat nasal bridge is typical.

options.label: C
options.explanation: About 40-50% have congenital heart disease, commonly AVSD and VSD.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Palpebral fissures slant upwards in Down's; downward slant suggests Treacher Collins or Noonan syndrome.

questions.pearl: Commonest congenital heart lesion in Down's syndrome: atrioventricular septal defect (endocardial cushion defect).

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery
questions.stem: Features of perforation of a hollow viscus:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Gangrene is tissue death from ischaemia; it may cause perforation but is not a feature of it.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Peritonitis following perforation causes anorexia, nausea and vomiting.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pain-limited shallow breathing and sepsis cause rapid respiration.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Peritonitis causes paralytic ileus with absolute constipation.

questions.pearl: Perforation: sudden severe pain, board-like rigidity, absent bowel sounds and free gas under the diaphragm on erect chest X-ray.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Green vegetables provide carotene (provitamin A); rich sources of preformed vitamin A are liver, fish liver oil, milk and eggs.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Sunflower oil is a rich source of vitamin E; B6 comes from meat, liver, whole grains and legumes.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Fish liver oil is the richest dietary source of vitamin D.

options.label: D
options.explanation: B12 is synthesised by bacteria and found only in animal foods, so strict vegans are at risk.

questions.pearl: Richest natural source of vitamin A and D: fish liver oil; vitamin E: vegetable oils such as sunflower and wheat germ oil.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Severe or persistent (irreversible) injury leads to cell death by necrosis or apoptosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Karyolysis is fading of nuclear chromatin due to DNase activity.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pyknosis is nuclear shrinkage with increased basophilia.

options.label: D
options.text: Karyorrhexis is structural fragmentation of nucleus
options.explanation: Karyorrhexis is fragmentation of the pyknotic nucleus; it is a standard nuclear change of necrosis.

questions.pearl: Nuclear changes in necrosis: pyknosis (shrinks), karyorrhexis (fragments), karyolysis (fades).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: The brain lacks conventional lymphatic vessels; CSF and the glymphatic system drain interstitial fluid.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Like the brain, the CNS parenchyma has no lymphatics.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The internal ear is classically listed among structures devoid of lymphatics.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The liver produces a large share of thoracic duct lymph via hepatic lymphatics.

questions.pearl: Structures without lymphatics: CNS, eyeball, internal ear, cartilage, epidermis, splenic pulp and bone marrow.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Citalopram is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Imipramine is a classic TCA, also used for nocturnal enuresis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Duloxetine is a serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor (SNRI).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Sertraline is an SSRI.

questions.pearl: TCAs: imipramine, amitriptyline, nortriptyline, clomipramine, doxepin; overdose causes QRS widening, treat with sodium bicarbonate.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Enalapril is a prodrug ACE inhibitor converted to enalaprilat.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fosinopril is an ACE inhibitor with dual renal and hepatic elimination.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Losartan is an angiotensin II AT1 receptor blocker (ARB).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Amlodipine is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker.

questions.pearl: ACE inhibitors end in -pril; their dry cough and angioedema are due to bradykinin accumulation, which ARBs avoid.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Insulin promotes glycogenesis and inhibits glycogenolysis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Insulin stimulates Na+/K+-ATPase, shifting potassium into cells; used to treat hyperkalaemia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Insulin inhibits hormone-sensitive lipase, reducing free fatty acid release.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Insulin suppresses hepatic gluconeogenesis.

questions.pearl: Insulin is the only hypoglycaemic hormone and the main anabolic hormone; it inhibits hormone-sensitive lipase.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Significant proteinuria (>150 mg/day) is abnormal and suggests glomerular or tubular disease.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Water is the main normal constituent of urine (about 95%).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Urea is the main normal organic solute in urine.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Creatinine is a normal constituent excreted daily in proportion to muscle mass.

questions.pearl: Abnormal urinary constituents: protein, glucose, ketone bodies, blood, bile salts and bile pigments.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Muscarinic stimulation causes miosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Muscarinic vagal effect causes bradycardia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Nicotinic stimulation of sympathetic ganglia and adrenal medulla can produce hypertension and tachycardia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: OPC causes excessive salivation; dry mouth suggests anticholinergic poisoning.

questions.pearl: Muscarinic features of OPC: DUMBELS - diarrhoea, urination, miosis, bronchorrhoea/bradycardia, emesis, lacrimation, salivation.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Cyclizine is a sedating first-generation H1 blocker used as an antiemetic.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Fexofenadine is a non-sedating second-generation antihistamine.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Promethazine is a highly sedating first-generation phenothiazine antihistamine.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cetirizine is a second-generation antihistamine with minimal CNS penetration.

questions.pearl: First-generation antihistamines cross the blood-brain barrier and are anticholinergic: sedation, dry mouth, urinary retention.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: GH deficiency impairs growth but is not immediately fatal.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Absolute insulin deficiency leads to fatal diabetic ketoacidosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Lack of PTH causes life-threatening hypocalcaemic tetany and laryngospasm.

options.label: D
options.explanation: TSH deficiency causes hypothyroidism, which is not acutely life-threatening.

questions.pearl: Classic life-saving hormones: aldosterone (mineralocorticoid), cortisol, PTH and insulin.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Paraproteins promote rouleaux formation, often giving ESR above 100 mm/h.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Raised fibrinogen and globulins in active RA increase the ESR.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Rising fibrinogen and physiological anaemia raise ESR in pregnancy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Increased red cell mass lowers the ESR.

questions.pearl: Low ESR: polycythaemia, sickle cell disease, spherocytosis, hypofibrinogenaemia and CCF.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Projectile, non-bilious vomiting of undigested food is typical.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Persistent vomiting and poor intake cause weight loss and dehydration.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Loss of HCl causes hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Gastric losses cause hyponatraemia, not hypernatraemia.

questions.pearl: Gastric outlet obstruction: hypochloraemic, hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis with paradoxical aciduria; correct with 0.9% saline plus KCl.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Beta blockers slow AV conduction and can precipitate complete heart block.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Beta blockers are first-line anti-anginal drugs (reduce heart rate and oxygen demand).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Non-selective beta blockers may cause bronchospasm; caution or avoidance in obstructive airway disease, absolute in asthma.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Topical beta blockers such as timolol are used to treat glaucoma.

questions.pearl: Beta blocker contraindications: asthma, heart block, decompensated heart failure, Prinzmetal angina, peripheral vascular disease.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Stable angina is relieved by rest, which reduces myocardial oxygen demand.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Calcium channel blockers reduce afterload and are used for angina.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Sublingual GTN relieves angina through venodilatation and reduced preload.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Combining nitrates with PDE-5 inhibitors causes severe, potentially fatal hypotension.

questions.pearl: Nitrates are contraindicated within 24 h of sildenafil (48 h for tadalafil).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Actions of the sympathetic nervous system:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Sympathetic activity inhibits gut motility and contracts sphincters; parasympathetic stimulates peristalsis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Beta-2 stimulation relaxes bronchial smooth muscle.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Alpha-1 stimulation contracts the radial (dilator pupillae) muscle causing mydriasis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Beta-1 stimulation of juxtaglomerular cells increases renin release.

questions.pearl: Sympathetic is fight or flight: mydriasis, tachycardia, bronchodilatation, reduced gut motility and increased renin.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pneumoconioses such as silicosis, asbestosis and coal worker's lung cause pulmonary fibrosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dust and fume exposure (coal, cotton, grain) contributes to occupational COPD.

options.label: C
options.explanation: TB is an infection; silicosis increases its risk, but TB itself is not classified as an occupational lung disease here.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Asbestos causes mesothelioma and bronchial carcinoma; arsenic, chromium and nickel are other occupational carcinogens.

questions.pearl: Asbestos: pleural plaques, mesothelioma and lung cancer; risk of lung cancer is multiplied by smoking.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fibrinogen is not vitamin K dependent.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Factor VI does not exist as a separate factor (it was found to be activated factor V).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Factor IX requires vitamin K-dependent gamma-carboxylation of glutamate residues.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Factor X is vitamin K dependent.

questions.pearl: Vitamin K-dependent factors: II, VII, IX, X and proteins C and S; warfarin blocks vitamin K epoxide reductase.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: VSD is an acyanotic left-to-right shunt; cyanosis appears only with Eisenmenger reversal.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A harsh pansystolic murmur at the left lower sternal edge is characteristic.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Large VSDs cause heart failure in infancy with sweating, especially during feeds.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Breathlessness during feeds causes poor feeding and failure to thrive.

questions.pearl: VSD is the commonest congenital heart disease; small (restrictive) defects have the loudest murmurs and often close spontaneously.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Reduced left ventricular filling lowers stroke volume, giving a small-volume pulse.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The palpable loud first heart sound gives a tapping apex beat.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Mitral leaflets are held wide open by high atrial pressure and close forcefully.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The mid-diastolic murmur of MS is low-pitched and rumbling, best heard with the bell in left lateral position.

questions.pearl: MS: loud S1, opening snap, low-pitched mid-diastolic rumble with presystolic accentuation (lost in AF).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Systemic-onset JIA has an evanescent salmon-pink rash with quotidian fever.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Carditis is a feature of rheumatic fever; JIA may cause pericarditis but carditis is not typical.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Joint swelling persisting at least 6 weeks is required for diagnosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Chronic synovitis leads to contractures, deformity and growth disturbance.

questions.pearl: Oligoarticular JIA with positive ANA carries a high risk of chronic anterior uveitis; screen with slit-lamp examination.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Haemolysis of parasitised and unparasitised red cells plus marrow suppression cause anaemia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Falciparum malaria causes hypoglycaemia, worsened by quinine-induced insulin release.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Haemolysis and hepatic dysfunction cause jaundice.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lactic acidosis from tissue hypoxia is a marker of severe malaria.

questions.pearl: Severe falciparum malaria: cerebral malaria, severe anaemia, hypoglycaemia, acidosis, AKI, pulmonary oedema; treat with IV artesunate.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery
questions.stem: Risk factors of colorectal cancer include:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Obesity and physical inactivity increase colorectal cancer risk.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dietary calcium is considered protective.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Selenium is an antioxidant thought to be protective, not a risk factor.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Diets high in red meat and saturated fat increase risk.

questions.pearl: Colorectal cancer risks: FAP, HNPCC, IBD, red/processed meat, smoking, obesity; protective: fibre, calcium, aspirin.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Causes of increased total RBC count (erythrocytosis):

options.label: A
options.explanation: Leukaemia infiltrates the marrow and causes anaemia, not erythrocytosis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Polycythaemia vera is a myeloproliferative neoplasm (JAK2 V617F) causing primary erythrocytosis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Chronic hypoxia (COPD, cyanotic heart disease) stimulates erythropoietin, causing secondary erythrocytosis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Low atmospheric oxygen at altitude drives EPO-mediated erythrocytosis.

questions.pearl: Secondary polycythaemia: high EPO from hypoxia or EPO-secreting tumours (renal cell carcinoma, hepatoma, cerebellar haemangioblastoma).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: About 20% of chronic HCV infection progresses to cirrhosis over 20-30 years.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Chronic HBV is a leading cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.

options.label: C
options.explanation: HEV is enterically transmitted and usually self-limiting; chronicity is very rare.

options.label: D
options.explanation: EBV may cause transient hepatitis in infectious mononucleosis but not cirrhosis.

questions.pearl: Viruses causing chronic hepatitis and cirrhosis: B, C and D (with B); A and E are faeco-oral and usually acute.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Breakthrough bleeding is common in the first few cycles, especially with low-dose pills.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Endometrial suppression causes lighter withdrawal bleeds.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Androgenic progestogens (e.g. levonorgestrel) and progestogen-only pills can cause acne.

options.label: D
options.explanation: OCPs thicken cervical mucus and reduce the risk of symptomatic PID.

questions.pearl: Serious OCP risks: venous thromboembolism, stroke, MI, hypertension and hepatic adenoma; benefits include reduced ovarian and endometrial cancer.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Pregnancy in the first trimester can be diagnosed by:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Transvaginal ultrasound shows a gestational sac at about 4.5-5 weeks.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Amenorrhoea in a sexually active woman is the earliest presumptive symptom.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Quickening is felt at 18-20 weeks (16-18 in multiparae), in the second trimester.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Urine or serum beta-hCG immunoassays detect pregnancy within days of a missed period.

questions.pearl: Earliest ultrasound evidence: gestational sac at about 5 weeks (TVS); cardiac activity at about 6 weeks.

questions.subject: Gynecology
questions.stem: Causes of bleeding in early pregnancy:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Twin pregnancy itself does not cause bleeding in early pregnancy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Miscarriage is the commonest cause of first-trimester bleeding.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Ectopic pregnancy presents with amenorrhoea, pain and vaginal bleeding.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hydatidiform mole classically presents with first-trimester bleeding and a uterus large for dates.

questions.pearl: Early pregnancy bleeding: abortion, ectopic pregnancy, molar pregnancy, implantation bleeding and local cervical lesions.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fast breathing and chest indrawing are the key signs of pneumonia in IMCI.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Bacterial pneumonia usually causes high fever with chills.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Cough is a cardinal symptom, often productive in older children and adults.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pneumonia causes tachycardia; relative bradycardia suggests atypical causes such as Legionella.

questions.pearl: IMCI fast breathing: 60 or more/min under 2 months, 50 or more at 2-12 months, 40 or more at 1-5 years.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.text: Commonly affects the posterior triangle of the neck
options.explanation: It arises from jugular lymph sacs and typically lies in the lower posterior triangle.

options.label: B
options.explanation: There is no significant sex predilection.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Intralesional sclerosants such as OK-432 or bleomycin are used; surgical excision is the alternative.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Large lesions extending to the floor of mouth or mediastinum may compress the airway.

questions.pearl: Cystic hygroma is brilliantly transilluminant, compressible and usually present at birth or before 2 years.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Supraglottic and advanced tumours spreading to the hypopharynx cause dysphagia.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Referred otalgia via the vagus (Arnold's nerve) is a feature of advanced disease.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Malignancy causes weight loss, not gain.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Anorexia and weight loss occur with advanced malignancy.

questions.pearl: Glottic carcinoma presents early with hoarseness and rarely spreads to nodes because the vocal cords have scant lymphatics.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Alcohol intake and withdrawal cause sinus tachycardia and AF (holiday heart).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hyperglycaemia itself does not cause tachycardia; hypoglycaemia does via adrenergic response.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hypothyroidism causes bradycardia; hyperthyroidism causes tachycardia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Digoxin toxicity causes tachyarrhythmias such as atrial tachycardia with block and ventricular tachycardia.

questions.pearl: Classic digoxin toxicity arrhythmia: paroxysmal atrial tachycardia with block; also bidirectional VT.

questions.subject: Obstetrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Prolonged pregnancy beyond 42 weeks raises the risk of placental insufficiency, meconium aspiration and stillbirth.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Elderly primigravida is listed as high risk because of higher rates of hypertension, diabetes and operative delivery.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Short stature suggests a contracted pelvis and risk of cephalopelvic disproportion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Multiple pregnancy increases preterm labour, pre-eclampsia, anaemia and PPH.

questions.pearl: High-risk pregnancy: extremes of age, short stature, bad obstetric history, multiple pregnancy, malpresentation, medical disorders, post-maturity.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Salpingitis damages tubal cilia and causes adhesions, the commonest risk factor.

options.label: B
options.explanation: DMPA suppresses ovulation, so ectopic pregnancy is very unlikely with it.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Endometrial hyperplasia does not predispose to ectopic implantation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Post-abortal and puerperal sepsis cause salpingitis and tubal damage, a recognised cause of ectopic pregnancy.

questions.pearl: Most common site of ectopic pregnancy: ampulla of the fallopian tube; isthmic ectopics rupture earliest.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pain in ASOM arises from the ear itself (primary otalgia).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dental and gum disease refer pain via the trigeminal (auriculotemporal) nerve.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Tongue lesions refer pain via the lingual (V3) and glossopharyngeal nerves.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Furunculosis of the external canal causes primary, local ear pain.

questions.pearl: Referred otalgia travels via cranial nerves V, VII, IX, X and C2-C3; always exclude a hidden pharyngeal or laryngeal cancer.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: AFP is raised in yolk sac tumours and many non-seminomatous germ cell tumours.

options.label: B
options.explanation: CA 19-9 is a marker for pancreatic and biliary cancer.

options.label: C
options.explanation: LDH reflects tumour burden and is used in staging.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Beta-hCG is raised in choriocarcinoma and some seminomas.

questions.pearl: Pure seminoma never raises AFP; a raised AFP means a non-seminomatous component.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Caused by HPV types 6 and 11, transmitted sexually.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hepatitis B (and less often C) is transmitted sexually and can become chronic.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Leprosy spreads by nasal droplets and prolonged close contact, not sexually.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Zoster is reactivation of latent varicella-zoster virus; genital herpes is caused by HSV.

questions.pearl: HPV 6 and 11 cause genital warts; HPV 16 and 18 cause cervical cancer.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Social smile appears at 6-8 weeks (about 2 months).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Head control is achieved by about 3 months.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Voluntary whole-hand (palmar) grasp of objects is established by about 5-6 months.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Bisyllabic babble (mama, dada) appears around 9 months.

questions.pearl: Milestones: social smile 2 months, neck holding 3 months, sits without support 8 months, walks alone 12-13 months.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Autoantibodies against platelet glycoproteins cause immune destruction.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Widespread microthrombi consume platelets and clotting factors.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Marrow suppression and immune destruction lower platelets, typically during the critical phase.

options.label: D
options.explanation: PV is a myeloproliferative neoplasm usually associated with raised platelets.

questions.pearl: ITP in children often follows a viral infection and resolves spontaneously; chronic adult ITP is commoner in women.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Man is the definitive host of:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Entamoeba histolytica completes its whole life cycle in man, its only (definitive) host.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Ascaris has a direct life cycle with man as the definitive host.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Man harbours the adult beef tapeworm (definitive host); cattle are the intermediate host.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Enterobius completes its life cycle in man alone.

questions.pearl: Man is intermediate host in echinococcosis (hydatid) and malaria; in T. solium man can be both definitive and intermediate host.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hereditary spherocytosis usually causes mild to moderate splenomegaly.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Chronic malaria and hyperreactive malarial splenomegaly cause massive splenomegaly.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Congestive splenomegaly in portal hypertension is usually moderate.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis causes moderate splenomegaly through portal hypertension.

questions.pearl: Massive splenomegaly: CML, myelofibrosis, chronic malaria, kala-azar, Gaucher disease, thalassaemia major.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.stem: Pathophysiology of peptic ulcer disease due to H. pylori:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Urease splits urea into ammonia, buffering acid around the organism; the basis of the urea breath test.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Antral H. pylori infection reduces somatostatin, raising gastrin and acid secretion in duodenal ulcer disease.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Infection reduces duodenal mucosal bicarbonate secretion, weakening mucosal defence.

options.label: D
options.explanation: CagA, VacA toxins and the inflammatory response damage the epithelium.

questions.pearl: H. pylori is found in about 90% of duodenal ulcers and 70% of gastric ulcers; eradicate with PPI plus two antibiotics.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: The inner ear is supplied by the labyrinthine artery.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The cornea is avascular, nourished by aqueous humour, tears and limbal vessels.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Testes are supplied by the testicular arteries from the aorta.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The lens is avascular and nourished by aqueous humour.

questions.pearl: Avascular tissues: cornea, lens, epidermis, hyaline cartilage, nails and hair; corneal avascularity underlies graft success.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Retinal vasculitis (e.g. Eales disease, SLE) causes haemorrhages.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Septicaemia and infective endocarditis cause retinal haemorrhages with white centres (Roth spots).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Hypertensive retinopathy causes flame-shaped haemorrhages (grade III).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Diabetic retinopathy causes dot-and-blot haemorrhages.

questions.pearl: Flame haemorrhages lie in the nerve fibre layer (hypertension, CRVO); dot-blot lie in deeper layers (diabetes).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: IBD is a non-infectious, immune-mediated cause of chronic diarrhoea.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Clostridioides difficile causes antibiotic-associated diarrhoea and pseudomembranous colitis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Colorectal cancer causes altered bowel habit but not infectious diarrhoea.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Enterotoxigenic E. coli is the commonest cause of travellers' diarrhoea.

questions.pearl: C. difficile risk: clindamycin, cephalosporins, fluoroquinolones; treat with oral vancomycin or fidaxomicin.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Most epistaxis is minor anterior bleeding from Little's area, controlled by pressure.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Haemorrhagic shock with coagulopathy leads to ongoing uncontrolled bleeding.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Uterine rupture causes massive intraperitoneal haemorrhage needing urgent laparotomy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Acidosis impairs clotting factor function, part of the lethal triad with hypothermia and coagulopathy.

questions.pearl: Lethal triad of trauma: hypothermia, acidosis and coagulopathy; damage control surgery aims to break it.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Repeated obstruction and inflammation cause chronic cholecystitis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Gallstones do not cause haematemesis; haemobilia is very rare.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Gallstones are the commonest cause of acute pancreatitis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Ascites is not a complication of gallstones.

questions.pearl: Gallstone complications: cholecystitis, empyema, mucocele, choledocholithiasis, cholangitis, pancreatitis, gallstone ileus, carcinoma.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: 5% dextrose is effectively free water; it does not expand plasma volume and worsens cerebral oedema in head injury.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Isotonic crystalloid is used for initial resuscitation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Warmed Ringer's lactate/Hartmann's is the preferred initial crystalloid in ATLS.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Glucose-containing fluids cause hyperglycaemia and are not recommended for trauma resuscitation.

questions.pearl: ATLS: 1 L warmed isotonic crystalloid initially, then early blood products in a 1:1:1 ratio for haemorrhagic shock.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: White patches in the throat are found in:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Streptococcal exudative tonsillitis gives white patches, with a white then red strawberry tongue.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Rubella causes Forchheimer spots (petechiae on the soft palate), not white patches.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Aphthous ulcers have a white-yellow fibrinous base with a red halo.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Fusospirochaetal infection produces a greyish-white membrane over an ulcerated tonsil.

questions.pearl: White patches in the throat: follicular tonsillitis, diphtheria, Vincent's angina, infectious mononucleosis, candidiasis, leukoplakia.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.text: Ground glass appearance of shaft of the bone
options.explanation: Ground glass appearance of the shaft is characteristic of scurvy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Cupping, splaying and fraying of the metaphysis are classic rachitic changes.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Corner (Pelkan) sign is a feature of scurvy.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Enlarged costochondral junctions are seen on chest X-ray as a rachitic rosary.

questions.pearl: Earliest X-ray sign of rickets: loss of the zone of provisional calcification at the wrist; best seen at the distal ulna.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Boas sign (hyperaesthesia below the right scapula) is seen in acute cholecystitis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Rovsing's sign suggests acute appendicitis.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Periumbilical bruising from retroperitoneal haemorrhage tracking along the falciform ligament.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Murphy's sign indicates acute cholecystitis.

questions.pearl: Haemorrhagic pancreatitis: Grey Turner's sign (flanks) and Cullen's sign (umbilicus); also Fox's sign (inguinal).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Renin is secreted by juxtaglomerular cells of the afferent arteriole.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Angiotensin II is formed mainly in the lung capillaries by ACE.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The renal medulla produces prostaglandins (PGE2, PGI2) that regulate renal blood flow.

options.label: D
options.explanation: ACTH is secreted by the anterior pituitary.

questions.pearl: Renal endocrine products: renin, erythropoietin, calcitriol (1-alpha hydroxylation) and prostaglandins.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Severe central crushing chest pain lasting over 20 minutes, unrelieved by GTN.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A clenched fist over the sternum describing ischaemic pain.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Weight loss is not a feature of acute MI.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Fatigue and weakness are common, especially in elderly, female and diabetic patients.

questions.pearl: Silent MI is commoner in diabetics and the elderly due to autonomic neuropathy.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Short-acting beta-2 agonists are reliever therapy at every step; LABA is added in later steps.

options.label: B
options.explanation: ICS is the cornerstone controller therapy.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Beta blockers cause bronchospasm and are contraindicated in asthma.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Leukotriene receptor antagonists are add-on controllers.

questions.pearl: Asthma steps: SABA, then low-dose ICS, then add LABA, then increase ICS or add LTRA/theophylline, then oral steroids or biologics.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Structures involved in the light reflex:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Parasympathetic preganglionic neurons for pupillary constriction arise here.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Postganglionic fibres arise in the ciliary ganglion and run in short ciliary nerves to the sphincter pupillae.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Light reflex fibres bypass the LGB and go to the pretectal nucleus.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The efferent limb travels in the oculomotor nerve.

questions.pearl: Light reflex: optic nerve (afferent), pretectal nucleus, Edinger-Westphal nucleus, oculomotor nerve, ciliary ganglion (efferent).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fever is common in viral meningitis.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Headache is a prominent symptom.

options.label: C
options.explanation: CSF glucose is normal in viral meningitis; it is low in bacterial and TB meningitis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Photophobia is a feature of meningeal irritation.

questions.pearl: Viral CSF: lymphocytes, normal glucose, mildly raised protein; bacterial: neutrophils, low glucose, high protein.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: A false cyst has a wall of fibrous or granulation tissue without an epithelial lining.

options.label: B
options.explanation: It contains fluid such as exudate, blood or pancreatic juice.

options.label: C
options.explanation: An organising haematoma may liquefy to form a false cyst.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Cysts from embryonic remnants (dermoid, branchial, thyroglossal) are true cysts.

questions.pearl: Classic false cyst: pancreatic pseudocyst, appearing about 4 weeks after acute pancreatitis in the lesser sac.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Staphylococci are catalase positive, distinguishing them from streptococci.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Coagulase positivity distinguishes S. aureus from coagulase-negative staphylococci.

options.label: C
options.explanation: S. aureus ferments mannitol, producing yellow colonies on mannitol salt agar.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Hyaluronidase is a spreading factor some strains produce, but it is not a routine identification test.

questions.pearl: S. aureus: catalase +, coagulase +, mannitol +, DNase +, golden-yellow pigment; MRSA is treated with vancomycin.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Interstitial fluid forms about three-quarters of the ECF.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Plasma forms about one-quarter of the ECF.

options.label: C
options.text: Acts as a positive feedback mechanism
options.explanation: ECF composition is regulated mainly by negative feedback to maintain homeostasis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: ECF glucose is held in a narrow range by insulin and counter-regulatory hormones.

questions.pearl: Total body water is 60% of body weight: two-thirds ICF, one-third ECF (interstitial 3/4, plasma 1/4).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Rebound anxiety and insomnia are common withdrawal symptoms.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Severe withdrawal can cause perceptual disturbances, hallucinations and delirium.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Autonomic hyperactivity during withdrawal causes tachycardia, palpitations and sweating.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Ataxia is a feature of benzodiazepine intoxication, not withdrawal.

questions.pearl: Benzodiazepine withdrawal can cause seizures; taper slowly, often switching to long-acting diazepam.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Acute anterior uveitis occurs in about 25-30% and is the commonest extra-articular feature.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Chronic prostatitis is a recognised association in men with AS.

options.label: C
options.explanation: AS is associated with IgA nephropathy and amyloidosis rarely, but glomerulonephritis is not a typical feature.

options.label: D
options.explanation: AS causes apical lung fibrosis; pulmonary nodules are a feature of rheumatoid arthritis.

questions.pearl: AS extra-articular A's: anterior uveitis, aortic regurgitation, apical fibrosis, amyloidosis, Achilles enthesitis, AV block.

questions.subject: Basic Sciences
questions.stem: Side effects of timolol eye drops:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Beta blockers are used for migraine prophylaxis rather than causing it.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Ocular stinging and burning on instillation are common local effects.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Topical beta blockers and preservatives can cause punctate keratopathy and dry eye.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Timolol lowers intraocular pressure by reducing aqueous production; it treats glaucoma.

questions.pearl: Systemic absorption of timolol drops can cause bronchospasm and bradycardia; press the nasolacrimal duct after instillation.

questions.subject: Obstetrics
questions.stem: Recurrent mid-trimester abortions occur due to:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Submucous fibroids distort the cavity and cause mid-trimester loss.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Gonorrhoea is not an established cause of recurrent mid-trimester miscarriage.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pre-eclampsia arises after 20 weeks and does not cause recurrent mid-trimester abortion.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Chronic maternal disease such as CKD impairs placentation and causes fetal loss.

questions.pearl: Commonest cause of recurrent mid-trimester painless abortion: cervical incompetence; treat with cervical cerclage.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.text: NSAIDs are used for pain relief
options.explanation: NSAIDs and aspirin increase bleeding risk and are avoided; paracetamol is used.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dengue virus (four serotypes) belongs to the Flaviviridae, transmitted by Aedes aegypti.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Dengue is a single-stranded RNA virus.

options.label: D
options.text: High haematocrit is a warning sign
options.explanation: Rising haematocrit with falling platelets indicates plasma leakage.

questions.pearl: Severe dengue risk is higher with secondary infection by a different serotype (antibody-dependent enhancement).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Increased capillary hydrostatic pressure (e.g. heart failure) causes oedema.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Reduced plasma oncotic pressure (hypoalbuminaemia) causes oedema.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Inflammation and burns increase permeability, producing exudative oedema.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Lymphatic obstruction (filariasis, malignancy, surgery) causes lymphoedema.

questions.pearl: Starling forces: oedema results from raised hydrostatic pressure, low oncotic pressure, increased permeability, lymphatic block or sodium retention.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.text: Swelling does not move with respiration
options.explanation: The kidney moves slightly downward with respiration.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A renal mass is bimanually palpable and ballotable because it lies against the posterior abdominal wall.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Fingers can be insinuated between a renal swelling and the costal margin (positive), unlike the spleen.

options.label: D
options.text: Long axis of the swelling is directed towards the opposite iliac fossa
options.explanation: This describes splenic enlargement, which grows towards the right iliac fossa.

questions.pearl: Renal swelling: ballotable, band of colonic resonance in front, fingers get above it; spleen has a notch and no resonance.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Wounds under tension heal poorly and dehisce more often.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Healing is slower in the elderly due to reduced collagen synthesis and blood supply.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Clean incised wounds heal faster than crushed, contaminated or lacerated ones.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Corticosteroids inhibit inflammation, fibroblast activity and collagen synthesis.

questions.pearl: Vitamin A partially reverses the delaying effect of steroids on wound healing.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Moon face with oedema is a feature of kwashiorkor; marasmic children have an old-man face.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Severe wasting of muscle and subcutaneous fat (skin and bones) is the hallmark.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Marasmic children usually have a good appetite; anorexia is typical of kwashiorkor.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Absence of oedema distinguishes marasmus from kwashiorkor.

questions.pearl: Kwashiorkor: oedema, apathy, flaky-paint dermatosis, fatty liver, flag sign; marasmus: wasting without oedema, alert and hungry.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Decontamination of skin and clothing prevents ongoing absorption and protects staff.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Atropine blocks muscarinic effects; titrate until the chest is clear and secretions dry.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Lavage may be considered in recent ingestion with a protected airway.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Flumazenil is a benzodiazepine antagonist, not used for OPC poisoning.

questions.pearl: Pralidoxime reactivates acetylcholinesterase if given before ageing; atropine endpoint is drying of bronchial secretions.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Glottic or subglottic tumour bulk narrows the airway.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Chronic laryngitis causes hoarseness rather than stridor.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Haemophilus influenzae type b epiglottitis causes rapidly progressive inspiratory stridor.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Juvenile recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (HPV 6, 11) causes hoarseness and stridor.

questions.pearl: Commonest cause of stridor in newborns and infants: laryngomalacia; in children: croup (laryngotracheobronchitis).

questions.subject: Basic Sciences

options.label: A
options.explanation: Thiamine is a water-soluble B vitamin.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Vitamin A is fat soluble and stored in the liver.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Pyridoxine is water soluble.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Vitamin K is fat soluble; deficiency occurs in fat malabsorption and obstructive jaundice.

questions.pearl: Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K; deficiency occurs in steatorrhoea and cholestasis.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Fracture of the talar neck disrupts retrograde blood supply to the body.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Intracapsular neck of femur fracture damages retinacular vessels.

options.label: C
options.explanation: The proximal pole is supplied retrogradely, so waist fractures risk AVN.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The humeral shaft is well vascularised; its typical complication is radial nerve palsy.

questions.pearl: AVN sites: femoral head, scaphoid proximal pole, talus body, capitulum, lunate (Kienbock) and second metatarsal head (Freiberg).

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Fluid of choice in severe dehydration:

options.label: A
options.explanation: Colloids such as albumin are not used for dehydration due to diarrhoea.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Ringer's lactate/Hartmann's is the preferred IV fluid for severe dehydration (WHO plan C).

options.label: C
options.explanation: Haemaccel is a gelatin colloid plasma expander, not used for rehydration.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Normal saline is an acceptable alternative when Ringer's lactate is unavailable.

questions.pearl: WHO plan C: 100 ml/kg Ringer's lactate; infants over 6 h (30 ml/kg in 1 h then 70 ml/kg in 5 h), older children over 3 h.

questions.subject: Gynecology

options.label: A
options.explanation: Adenomyosis causes progressive secondary dysmenorrhoea with a bulky, tender uterus.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Submucous fibroids cause congestive and spasmodic dysmenorrhoea.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Anovulatory DUB is typically painless.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Endometriosis is a leading cause of secondary dysmenorrhoea.

questions.pearl: Primary dysmenorrhoea is due to prostaglandin excess in ovulatory cycles; first-line treatment is NSAIDs.

questions.subject: Pediatrics

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pneumonia is the commonest cause of measles-related death.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Otitis media is the commonest complication.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Diarrhoea is common and contributes to malnutrition.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Measles does not cause intestinal obstruction.

questions.pearl: Late complication of measles: subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) years later; give vitamin A to all cases.

questions.subject: General Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Stored blood lacks functional platelets and labile factors, causing dilutional coagulopathy.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Rapid infusion of cold stored blood causes hypothermia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Citrate binds calcium, causing hypocalcaemia.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Citrate overload chelates calcium, causing tetany and myocardial depression.

questions.pearl: Massive transfusion: hypocalcaemia, hyperkalaemia, hypothermia, coagulopathy, acidosis then alkalosis, and TRALI.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Acute gout causes excruciating pain, typically in the first MTP joint (podagra).

options.label: B
options.explanation: Gout is an intense inflammatory crystal arthritis driven by neutrophils and IL-1.

options.label: C
options.text: NSAIDs are contraindicated in the acute state
options.explanation: NSAIDs (or colchicine, steroids) are first-line for acute gout.

options.label: D
options.text: Presence of tophi may be found
options.explanation: Chronic tophaceous gout produces urate deposits in ears, olecranon and fingers.

questions.pearl: Gout crystals are needle-shaped and negatively birefringent; do not start allopurinol during an acute attack.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Detrusor overactivity causes sudden urgency.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Haematuria is not a feature of an irritable bladder and needs investigation for stone, tumour or infection.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Small-volume frequent voiding is typical.

options.label: D
options.explanation: A poor stream indicates outflow obstruction such as stricture or BPH.

questions.pearl: Overactive bladder: urgency with or without urge incontinence, usually with frequency and nocturia; treat with bladder training and antimuscarinics.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Hepatic vein outflow obstruction causes portal hypertension with ascites and splenomegaly.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Kala-azar causes massive splenomegaly, but ascites is not a characteristic feature.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Malaria causes splenomegaly without ascites.

options.label: D
options.text: Cirrhosis of liver with portal hypertension
options.explanation: Portal hypertension causes congestive splenomegaly, and with hypoalbuminaemia produces ascites.

questions.pearl: SAAG of 1.1 g/dl or more indicates portal hypertensive ascites (cirrhosis, Budd-Chiari, cardiac ascites).

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Pruritus, worse at night, is due to hypersensitivity to the mite and its products.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Scratching produces secondary eczematisation and impetiginisation.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Silvery scales are characteristic of psoriasis.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Pinpoint bleeding on scraping scales is a sign of psoriasis.

questions.pearl: Scabies burrows favour finger webs, wrists, genitalia; treat patient and all contacts with permethrin 5%.

questions.subject: Medicine

options.label: A
options.explanation: Heavy proteinuria and hypoalbuminaemia lower oncotic pressure.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Hypoalbuminaemia and sodium retention cause ascites and generalised oedema.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Low plasma proteins reduce oncotic pressure from any cause (malnutrition, malabsorption).

options.label: D
options.explanation: Left heart failure causes pulmonary oedema; right heart failure causes generalised dependent oedema.

questions.pearl: Anasarca causes: congestive (right) heart failure, nephrotic syndrome, cirrhosis, malnutrition and protein-losing enteropathy.

questions.subject: Specialized Surgery

options.label: A
options.explanation: Caustic injury causes immediate painful dysphagia and later stricture.

options.label: B
options.explanation: Dysphagia from a post-cricoid web is chronic and intermittent, with iron deficiency anaemia.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Diffuse oesophageal spasm causes sudden episodic dysphagia with chest pain.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Boerhaave syndrome causes sudden pain, dysphagia and surgical emphysema after vomiting.

questions.pearl: Boerhaave syndrome: vomiting followed by chest pain and surgical emphysema (Mackler's triad); rupture is usually left posterolateral lower oesophagus.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.stem: Total thyroidectomy may injure the following structures:

options.label: A
options.explanation: The internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve runs through the thyrohyoid membrane, away from the operative field.

options.label: B
options.explanation: It lies in the tracheo-oesophageal groove near the inferior thyroid artery; injury causes hoarseness or stridor.

options.label: C
options.explanation: It runs close to the superior thyroid pedicle; injury paralyses cricothyroid, causing voice fatigue and loss of high pitch.

options.label: D
options.explanation: Inadvertent removal or devascularisation causes postoperative hypocalcaemia.

questions.pearl: Ligate the superior thyroid artery close to the gland to protect the external laryngeal nerve; ligate the inferior thyroid artery away from it to protect the RLN.
